sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Hazleton, PA?
sections.html:
Hazleton is a compact, fast-changing city in Luzerne County where homes are affordable and about half are rented. The Census Bureau estimates 30,286 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,340 in the 2010 census and 29,963 in 2020.

For 2020 to 2024 the Census lists a 51.1 percent owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $151,600 and median gross rent of $1,089. Median household income was $46,177, 63.4 percent of residents identify as Hispanic or Latino, 38.0 percent were born outside the United States, and 57.8 percent of residents age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home. The city itself publishes major notices in English and Spanish.

Sellers here include longtime owners of older rowhouses, landlords with several units and heirs to a house they do not plan to keep. If a buyer or tenant speaks mainly Spanish, plan for bilingual paperwork and a translator at the closing table.

sections.h2: Where is Hazleton and how does its setting affect a house?
sections.html:
Hazleton sits on a plateau called Spring Mountain in northeastern Pennsylvania, 35 miles northwest of Allentown, 82 miles north-northwest of Philadelphia and 106 miles west of New York City. The city covers 5.97 square miles, all land, and Wikipedia gives its highest point as 1,886 feet, which makes it the highest incorporated city in the state. It straddles the divide between the Delaware and Susquehanna River watersheds.

Height brings weather. The climate is warm-summer humid continental, with about 47 inches of snow and 50 inches of rain a year. The city's building codes list a frost depth of 42 inches, a ground snow load of 40 pounds per square foot and a design wind load of 115 miles per hour. Buyers and inspectors in Hazleton look closely at roofs, chimneys, gutters, foundations and basement moisture, so a recent repair record helps.

sections.h2: How did Hazleton's coal history shape its housing?
sections.html:
Anthracite built Hazleton. Coal was found at nearby Beaver Meadows in 1818, the Hazleton Coal Company was incorporated in 1836, the town became a borough on January 5, 1857 and a city on December 4, 1891. Small company towns called patches grew around it, including Jeddo, Stockton, Jeansville, Tresckow and Freeland.

  • German and Irish immigrants arrived in the 1840s and 1850s.
  • Italian, Polish, Russian, Lithuanian, Slovak and Montenegrin workers followed from the 1860s to the 1920s.
  • Since the early 2000s, new residents from the Dominican Republic and New York and New Jersey have reshaped the city again.

The result is a housing stock of narrow, older homes on steep, close lots. Many have been in a family for generations, which is why a good number of Hazleton sales involve an estate, several heirs or a house with deferred maintenance.

sections.h2: What does Hazleton's economy and transportation look like?
sections.html:
Mining and garment work have mostly disappeared. Distribution and manufacturing now dominate through the Humboldt Industrial Park in neighboring Hazle Township, where employers have included Amazon, Coca-Cola, American Eagle Outfitters, Hershey, General Mills and Steelcase. Mean travel time to work is 21.3 minutes.

Three interstates reach the area: I-80, I-81 and I-476, the Northeast Extension of the Pennsylvania Turnpike. Five state routes enter the city: PA 93 on Broad Street, PA 309 on Church Street, PA 424, PA 924 and PA 940. Hazleton Public Transit runs nine routes through the city and surrounding towns, and jitney companies run to Stroudsburg and New York City via I-80.

The Hazleton Area School District serves the city, with Hazleton Elementary/Middle, Heights-Terrace Elementary/Middle and Arthur Street Elementary inside city limits and Hazleton Area High School in Hazle Township. Greater Hazleton, which includes parts of Luzerne, Schuylkill and Carbon counties, had 77,187 residents in 2010.

sections.h2: What city rules apply to Hazleton rentals, permits and inspections?
sections.html:
Several Hazleton rules can affect how a sale closes, and City Hall at 570-459-4960 can point you to the Code Enforcement Office. Residential rental units must be registered with the Code Enforcement Office within 30 days of a new owner taking title, with one application and one license per property.

  • An owner who lives more than 10 air miles outside the city must appoint an agent who lives within 10 air miles.
  • Building permits are required for interior renovation, new siding, a new roof, sidewalks, sheds, fences, paving and concrete work.
  • Residential permit applications can take up to 15 days, and all outstanding fees and fines, including property taxes, garbage, water and sewer, must be paid before a permit is issued.
  • A residential zoning permit costs $75 per unit and takes about 15 days.

sections.h2: Can the Hazleton Land Bank or code violations affect my sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the house is vacant, blighted or tax-delinquent. The City of Hazleton Land Bank exists to return vacant, abandoned and tax-delinquent properties to productive use, and it meets on the first and third Wednesdays of the month. Ask City Hall whether any code or fee balance is attached to your property before you sign a sale contract.

Hazleton voters approved a Home Rule Charter in the November 3, 2026 general election. Call the Code Enforcement Office to confirm whether the charter changes any permit or inspection step that applies to your sale.

sections.h2: How are recording and transfer tax handled in Luzerne County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Hazleton houses go to the Luzerne County Recorder of Deeds. Pennsylvania charges a 1 percent state realty transfer tax on the value of the real estate, and county recorders collect a local share as well. Both grantor and grantee are jointly liable, so your closing statement should show how the cost is split.

Transfers by will or intestate succession are exempt, which helps an heir who is transferring a house into their own name. The Department of Revenue's valuation factor for Luzerne County is 1.14 for documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Ask the Recorder's office or your title company for the exact local rate and current recording fees.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a Hazleton house?
sections.html:
Most Hazleton owners choose among three paths.

  • List with an agent for a house in sound condition and a seller who can wait for financing and inspections.
  • Sell by owner to save the commission, handling pricing, showings and contracts yourself.
  • Accept a cash offer for an inherited, vacant, damaged or tenant-occupied house, with an as-is purchase and a closing date you choose.

Add up repairs, taxes owed, rental registration items and holding costs before you decide.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a Hazleton rental when I buy it?
faqs.a: Yes. Residential rental units must be registered with the City's Code Enforcement Office within 30 days of becoming the owner. If you live outside a 10-mile air radius of the city, you must appoint an agent who lives inside it.

faqs.q: Can I get a building permit in Hazleton if I owe city bills?
faqs.a: No. The city says all outstanding fees and fines, including property taxes, garbage, water and sewer, must be paid before a permit is issued.

faqs.q: How much is a Hazleton occupancy inspection?
faqs.a: It is $75 per dwelling unit when scheduled 15 days ahead, $150 with shorter notice and $300 within 72 hours. Extra copies of the certificate cost $5, and a no-show adds $50.

faqs.q: Is an inherited house in Hazleton subject to transfer tax?
faqs.a: A transfer by will or intestate succession is exempt from Pennsylvania realty transfer tax. A later sale by the heirs to a buyer is a separate transfer and carries the 1 percent state tax plus the local share.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Hazleton homes?
faqs.a: The Hazleton Area School District covers the city. Three of its schools are inside city limits, and Hazleton Area High School is in Hazle Township.
